name: IC-7100
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not an Icom publication and not affiliated with Icom.
verified: Compiled from the Icom IC-7100 Instruction Manual and published specifications, September 2026. Not checked against a radio. Figures adjusted to the US model. The reset procedures could not be read and are left out.
specs: HF, 6 m, 2 m and 70 cm. US models have no 4 m band
USB, LSB, CW, RTTY, AM, FM, DV. WFM receive only
2 to 100 W on HF and 6 m, 2 to 50 W on 2 m, 2 to 35 W on 70 cm
13.8 V DC plus or minus 15 per cent
22 A on HF and 6 m, 16 A on 2 m and 70 cm
1.2 A at full audio, 0.9 A standby
Two SO-239. One for HF and 6 m, one for 2 m and 70 cm
Main unit about 2.3 kg, controller about 0.5 kg
None. An external AH-4, AT-180 or AH-740 is the option
USB port, and a remote jack
keys: Push on, hold about a second off. Rotate for volume.
Cycles the touch key sets, M-1 to M-3. It does not open a settings tree.
Opens the quick menu. Push again to close.
There is no EXIT key on this radio. Back out with MENU or the return symbol on screen.
Selects memories, or drives passband and offset when those are active.
One shared display for mic gain and transmit power.
Keyer speed, roughly 6 to 48 words per minute, and CW pitch, roughly 300 to 900 Hz.
Push announces the frequency and meter. Hold about a second for lock.
External tuner, or the call channel.
The receiver conditioning keys, as printed.
quick: The row you will use most: split, VFO swap, memory write.
DUP, AGC, TONE, DSQL, VOICE, KEYER, DEC, COMP, RTTY, CS, TBW
Repeater shift and tone live here, along with AGC and the keyer.
MEMO, SCOPE, SWR, DTMF, VOX, BK-IN
Break-in and the standing wave meter.
The repeater rows in DR mode.
tasks: The memory write key in the first touch row.
V/M in the first touch row. The channel knob steps channels.
The scan key in the first touch row.
The split key in the first touch row.
The mic and power key, then adjust.
In FM, the shift and tone keys in the second touch row.
control: The remote jack on the rear, or over USB
Selectable from 300 up to 19200, or auto. Write yours below
A CT-17 is needed for the remote jack. USB does CI-V with no converter
notes: No internal tuner, despite the size of it. Whatever you put up has to be resonant or matched by something you carried in.
Two antenna sockets, and the wrong one is the first thing to check when a band seems dead.
There is no EXIT key. If you are used to an IC-7300 you will hunt for it.
Twenty-two amps on HF. Size the supply for that even if you never run it.
The detachable head is a connector, and connectors fail. Carry the spare cable.
settings: CI-V address, as read from set mode
